changes.title: Arm the dormant hedge/defense sleeve on book-breadth triggers, not just SPY falling reads
changes.rationale: Aug 18 (-$26,844, worst day) ran ~3.9x down-capture (book -2.63% vs SPY -0.68%) with 11 NAME FALLING reads fired, yet every index-level defense executed zero trades: core_defense_fires_window=0, auto_hedge=flat every cycle, puts_approved=0 — because _market_falling()/_apply_core_defense/_apply_auto_hedge (orchestrator.py:851-968) key on an INDEX falling read and SPY never fell past -1.1% intraday. The failed Aug 3-21 down-capture of 2.306 is single-name reversals on flattish SPY, exactly the case the current trigger cannot see. HEDGE_ETF=PSQ is already configured (.env:219) and never fires.
changes.expected_effect: PSQ auto-hedge (30% of net-long) and core-DCA suppression actually engage on calm-tape red days, offsetting roughly a third of the beta bleed; the -$23.8k unrealized-marks pattern of Aug 18 shrinks materially; the bearish sleeve finally produces protection without depending on the 0/83 LLM put funnel.
changes.risk: Whipsaw: Aug 19 bounced +$19,336 the next day (CDE 75% of it), so a hedge opened late Aug 18 gives some back; PSQ (inverse QQQ) has basis mismatch vs small-cap losers. Bound it with the existing 2-cycle min and 15% cap.
changes.measurement: Grep BEARISH FUNNEL lines: auto_hedge must show armed/open on any day with >=3 concurrent NAME FALLING reads or day P/L <= -1.25%; compare down-capture on SPY-down days in the next 2-week window vs 2.306.

changes.title: Revert sizing to the documented defensive profile: KELLY_FRACTION 1.0->0.5, TARGET_ANNUAL_VOL_PCT 45->25
changes.rationale: The Jul 27 aggressive profile (.env:157-158, comments literally say 'was 0.5' / 'was 25') is the sizing floor under the bleed: worst day -$26,844 = 2.7% of equity on a -0.68% SPY day, avg loss -$2,485, profit factor only 1.098 — the book cannot afford 2.3x down-capture at this gross. Size = min(LLM weight, vol-target/Kelly, 12%) per risk._evaluate_buy, so this de-levers mechanically. Research digest: vol-scaled sizing is significant precisely in the momentum subset (8/103 Cederburg portfolios) this book belongs to, and regime/vol de-grossing beats bought puts (PPUT = pure drag) for down-capture.
changes.expected_effect: Per-position notionals roughly halve where the vol-target term binds; red-day mark-to-market losses scale down proportionally (an Aug 18-type day lands near -$13k instead of -$27k) while PF and win rate are unchanged; max drawdown (-2.98% this cycle) compresses.
changes.risk: Cuts up-capture too (already only 1.19 Aug 3-21) and halves dollar expectancy per trade; this is the deliberate risk-first trade while capture ratio is failing.
changes.measurement: Median new-entry notional in trades.jsonl vs this window; worst-day P/L as % of equity; up/down capture pair for the new window — success is down-capture <=1.3 with up-capture >=0.7.

changes.title: Close the options bypass: apply the anti-chase/overextension gate inside evaluate_option and cap per-underlying premium at 0.5% equity
changes.rationale: HL is the smoking gun: equity buy blocked by the overextension gate (RSI 70, 4.2xATR) and the same cycle expressed the identical thesis as a $5,200 bull call spread that lost -67.6% in 20.5 hours — the autotune agent's own finding: 'options are an unguarded bypass of the overextension gate.' Options are the cycle's loss engine: -$22,149 across 5 closes vs equity +$29,180, bull_call_spread 0-for-4 (-$33,794), and AMZN concentrated ~$29.8k premium in one underlying (-$14,956, the single biggest loss). risk.evaluate_option (risk.py:903-1038) has DTE/liquidity/premium gates but no anti-chase gate; autotune sweeps zero options knobs so this loss channel is invisible to the self-tuner.
changes.expected_effect: Overextended-name option entries (the HL/SMCI pattern) get blocked or haircut like their equity twins; no single underlying can hold >$5k premium at current equity, capping the AMZN-class tail at roughly a third of its realized size.
changes.risk: The lone option winner (MSFT long call +$11,645) might have been haircut; the gate blocks some legitimate momentum expressions. Given 0-for-4 spreads, acceptable.
changes.measurement: Next window: zero option entries on names simultaneously rejected as overextended (grep paired REJECT/option lines); max per-underlying premium in trades.jsonl <=0.5% equity; options sleeve P&L vs -$18,606 away-window baseline.

changes.title: Harden watchdog premium-stop marks: 2-tick confirmation + quote sanity + post-open suppression window
changes.rationale: The HL premium stop executed at -67.6% vs its -50% width 14 seconds after the open while the underlying traded UP — the Jul 23 junk one-sided-quote failure mode resurfacing on EXIT marks (PR #40 hardened entries only). That single artifact was -$3,650 = 30% of Aug 20's -$11,970. Overshoot was 17.6pp past the configured OPTION_STOP_LOSS_PCT=50 floor (watchdog.py:715 fires on a single 30s-tick mark).
changes.expected_effect: Premium stops require two consecutive ticks beyond threshold with a two-sided NBBO inside the 10% spread cap, and are suppressed for the first ~5 minutes after open unless the underlying itself moved adversely — eliminating open-auction phantom stops while keeping genuine collapse exits within ~60s.
changes.risk: On a true gap-down the extra tick adds ~30s of slippage; bounded because spreads are defined-risk (max loss = debit).
changes.measurement: No premium stop in the next window executes >5pp past its configured width inside the first 15 minutes after open; log shows suppressed-then-cleared events instead of instant fires.

changes.title: Add NAME_DROP_DEFENSE_PCT=2.5 to .env (from config-default 4.0)
changes.rationale: The name-drop defense works when it fires (Aug 18 cuts INTC/MTRN/IESC all kept falling after exit) but arms too late: SPCX bled -2.0% and -2.6% on Aug 18/19 — each under the 4% daily bar — then exited -8.9%; INTC's read armed at -4.5% but the exit came 52 minutes later at -5.8% (-1.3pp cadence cost); MTRN gave back -8.4% from high-water with the 1.5R trail never armed. All cuts landed 0.7-4.2pp before hard stops — the leak is read latency, not stop width. The knob exists only as config.py:474/830 default and is absent from .env, so this is a pure knob-add per the config agent's instruction.
changes.expected_effect: Defense reads arm 1-1.5pp earlier and catch two-day drip patterns on day one, converting -8 to -9% exits into -4 to -6% exits; directly shaves the unrealized-marks component that made Aug 18 89% mark-driven.
changes.risk: More reads feed Claude decision exits, which already net -$24,695 over 23 closes, and churn like the F sell/re-buy (~$425); mitigated by the existing rotation-guard red-day release and 24h re-entry cooldown.
changes.measurement: Count NAME FALLING reads and average exit depth below position high-water for defense-cut names (target: no cut deeper than -6% from HW); track re-buys within 48h of a defense exit as churn cost.

changes.title: Corroboration gate in risk._evaluate_buy: block or halve new-name buys cited on a single soft signal family
changes.rationale: Insider-cited entries are the worst family: 13 trades, -$18,681 (-$1,437/trade); the uncorroborated single-signal cohort (QNT -$1,621, LFTO -$1,634, INTC -$2,085, F -$842, AVBC -$493) lost ~-$6,675 and these junk small-caps are the same names driving red-day marks (composite Q4 >=2.02 expectancy -$859 cycle / -$1,792 away). Autotune's own conclusion must be respected: conviction-floor sweeps showed 0 trades affected at every candidate — 'the fix needs a new corroboration/multi-signal gate, not knob tightening.' Insert after the new-name floor in risk._evaluate_buy (risk.py:276-900): new names citing only insider or only options_flow (no fundamentals/news/technical corroboration) are blocked unless composite >=1.25, else starter-haircut x0.5. Corroborated names won: SMCI +$9,437, AXTI +$7,632, CDE +$15,860.
changes.expected_effect: Removes or halves the fast-failing single-signal cohort (~-$6.7k/window realized plus its red-day mark contribution) while leaving the fundamentals/news winners (+$28,983 and +$27,377 cycle) untouched.
changes.risk: Occasional single-signal winner blocked; overlap with the expectancy gate (which blocks only when ALL cited families are negative) must be checked so names aren't double-haircut. Small added prompt/gate complexity.
changes.measurement: Ledger attribution next window: count gate rejections/haircuts, then compute realized P&L of the would-have-been-blocked cohort — gate succeeds if that cohort's expectancy is negative while overall trade count drops <20%.

diagnosis: The book's problem is not expectancy (+$167/trade, PF 1.098, 42 trips) but drawdown geometry: Aug 3-21 down-capture is 2.306 vs up-capture 1.189, and the worst day (Aug 18, -$26,844) was ~89% unrealized marks across 13 held names at 3.9x SPY on a -0.68% SPY day. Every index-level defense sat at zero — core defense 0 fires, PSQ auto-hedge flat all window, bearish funnel 0-for-83 — because they all key on SPY falling reads that never trip on calm-tape red days, while the sizing profile runs full Kelly at a 45% vol target (the 'aggressive' Jul 27 overrides). The options sleeve is a second independent bleed: -$22,149 cycle with bull call spreads 0-for-4 (-$33,794), the HL entry explicitly routing around the equity overextension gate and then being stopped -67.6% vs a -50% width on a junk 14-seconds-post-open mark. Per-name defenses genuinely work (expectancy-gate rejects saved ~$17k+ on KALU/AEHR; Aug 18 cuts kept falling after exit) but arm too late — the 4% daily read floor plus 52-min cadence costs 0.7-4.2pp per cut. So the plan is: make the existing hedge/defense machinery fire on book-breadth, de-lever the base sizing, close the options bypass and its phantom-stop marks, and arm the name-drop defense earlier.
do_not_do: Do not chase single-name put conversion by prompt persuasion or by loosening put liquidity gates: 82/83 declines cited genuine contradicting bullish call flow, the one organic proposal (MARA) would have lost (+7.7%/+15.5% next sessions), and the research digest's strongest negative finding is that bought index puts are pure drag (PPUT = 36.5/63.5 equity-cash mix) — deterministic de-grossing/PSQ hedging is the evidence-backed route.

Do not tighten equity stop widths per curated.md line 14: the two 'stop failure' lessons (AMZN -$14,956, HL -$3,650) were watchdog OPTION premium stops misattributed by the postmortem; equity defense cuts landed 0.7-4.2pp BEFORE hard stops, so DEFAULT_STOP_LOSS_PCT=8 is not the leak.

Do not bump decision cadence or touch DECISION_INTERVAL_SECONDS=3120 this window: it is tuned to the 1h prompt-cache TTL ($0.192/cycle economics), and the walk-forward math needs 21-33 frozen trades (~2.5-3.3 weeks) per verdict — a cadence change would confound the 2-week test of these six changes.

Do not read the away-week capture flip (up 2.03 / down 1.71 over only 3 up / 4 down days) as evidence the down-capture problem self-resolved: the Aug 3-21 window still fails at 2.306 and Aug 18 ran 3.9x — the sample is far too small and the mechanism (dormant defenses) is unchanged.
lens: RISK-FIRST: cut red-day bleed and fix drawdown geometry (down-capture 2.31 is the #1 problem)

diagnosis: Ledger and independent recompute agree exactly (cycle 42 closes / +$7,030.97 / +$167.40 per trade; away 18 / +$3,402.85 / +$189.05), so the numbers are trustworthy, and the away-window equity drop (-$10.7k) is unrealized marks, not closed-trade losses. The book earns through payoff asymmetry (avg win $6,083 vs avg loss -$2,485 at 31% win rate), and essentially all gross profit comes from two places: mechanical exits (trail +$28,674 + bracket_take +$35,197 + take +$11,645 = +$75.5k) and fundamentals/news-cited entries (+$28,983 + $27,377). Three identifiable leaks consumed almost all of it: bull call spreads 0-for-4 (-$33,794), Claude discretionary decision exits (23 of 42 closes, net -$24,695), and insider-cited entries (13 trades, -$18,681, -$1,437 each). Composite is anti-predictive at the top (Q4 >=2.02 expectancy -$859 cycle / -$1,792 away vs Q3 +$2,728) and autotune proved conviction floors touch 0 losing trades, so the alpha fix lives in signal composition, exit ownership, and entry timing — not in knob floors. Expectancy collapsed 87% vs the pre-eval not because winners shrank (avg win held ~$6k) but because the leak channels fired more often; plugging them while enlarging winners (up-capture 0.80 pre-eval says exits are premature; the vetoed CDE top-up cost $7-12k) is the highest-leverage path.

changes.title: Corroboration gate: block new-name buys whose only cited signal family is insider/congress (risk._evaluate_buy)
changes.rationale: Insider-cited entries are the worst family: 13 trades, -$18,681 (-$1,437/trade), vs fundamentals +$28,983/26 and news +$27,377/6. The autotune digest is explicit that conviction floors cannot express this fix (every sweep candidate 0.35-0.6 affected 0 trades; QNT -$1,621 and LFTO -$1,634 entered insider-only at conviction >0.6 and died same-day; uncorroborated single-soft-signal entries totaled -$6,675). The Q4 composite losers (FTK, QNT, LFTO, FCEL) are the same junky single-source names, so this also attacks the -$859/trade top-quartile inversion without arming a composite floor.
changes.expected_effect: Removes a ~-$1,400/trade family from the entry mix (~5-8 trades per 2-week window), reallocating cycle-budget dollars toward fundamentals/news-corroborated names that earned +$1,100-4,500/trade; roughly +$5-8k expectancy improvement per window.
changes.risk: Kills some future insider-anchored winners if drawn too wide — the gate must key on 'insider/congress is the ONLY cited family', not 'insider is cited' (SMCI +$9,437 and CDE +$15,860 cited insider among corroborating families). Shrinks trade count, lengthening the stats clock.
changes.measurement: Next-run ledger attribution: count of entries whose cited set is insider-only should be 0; cycle_cited_insider P&L per trade should move toward flat; overall expectancy vs the +$167 baseline with trade count noted.

changes.title: Winner protection: veto Claude decision-SELLs on green positions below trail-arm unless a NAME FALLING read is armed
changes.rationale: Decision exits are 55% of all closes (23 of 42) and net -$24,695 (-$1,074 each), while the bot's own mechanical exits netted +$75,516 (trail +$28,674/5, bracket_take +$35,197/5, take +$11,645) — and pre-eval up-capture was 0.80, i.e. exits premature. The red-day autopsy validated the loss-cut side (INTC/MTRN/IESC kept falling after exit), so the veto must apply only to in-profit names that have not reached the 1.5R TRAIL_ARM_R threshold, with the existing NAME_DROP_DEFENSE_PCT=4.0 read and earnings blackout as releases. Implemented next to the rotation guard in the orchestrator sell path (orchestrator.py:1776 region), leaving watchdog hard stops untouched.
changes.expected_effect: Shifts winner exits from discretionary to trail/bracket machinery, raising avg win above $6,083 and up-capture above 0.80; eliminates the F-style churn round-trip ($425) and premature green closes.
changes.risk: A green name can round-trip to red while the veto holds (IESC gave back $6.7k on Aug 18 as a held gainer) — bounded by the hard 2-sigma stop and the NAME FALLING release; needs the postmortem give-back blindness fixed separately or lessons will mislabel the outcome.
changes.measurement: Exit-reason mix next run: decision-exit share of closes falls from 55%, trail+bracket_take share of gross profit rises from its current ~81%; avg win vs $6,083 baseline; up-capture vs 0.80/1.19.

changes.title: Halve decision cadence: DECISION_INTERVAL_SECONDS 3120 -> 1560
changes.rationale: The cadence-bump precondition the user set (cache_read>0) has been satisfied every trading day since Jul 23 (6-10 cache-hit calls/day, 43-73k cache tokens) and sat unacted-on for a month. Hourly cadence has measured alpha cost: INTC's NAME FALLING read armed at -4.5% but the exit came 52 minutes later at -5.8% (-1.3pp), MTRN gave back -7.7% in one morning between cycles, SPCX bled to -8.9% via sub-threshold drips. Cost math: $0.192/decision observed, so doubling from 8 to ~15 calls/day costs ~$1.50/day extra (~$30/mo) against a 209:1 P&L-to-spend ratio; 1560s stays comfortably inside the 1h prompt-cache TTL the interval was tuned for.
changes.expected_effect: Cuts read-to-exit and read-to-entry latency roughly in half (~26 min worst case), recovering the 1-2pp/incident inter-cycle slippage on both defense exits and momentum entries; also doubles top-up/trail-management touchpoints for winners.
changes.risk: More cycles = more discretionary decision opportunities (the negative-expectancy exit channel) — mitigated by the winner-protection veto shipping in the same window; API spend roughly doubles (still <$50/mo).
changes.measurement: api_usage.jsonl shows ~15-16 decision calls/trading day at ~$0.19/call with cache_read>0 preserved; grep logs for NAME FALLING read-to-exit gap (target <30 min); expectancy vs baseline.

changes.title: Open-auction hygiene: arm the open-bell cycle at 10:00 ET and ignore first-15-minute option premium-stop marks (orchestrator.py:806 + watchdog.py)
changes.rationale: Entry timing is structurally worst-practice: the guaranteed at-open-bell cycle plus daily caps concentrate fresh entries in 13:30-14:30 UTC, exactly the window the evidence digest grades as noise (JFE 2018: only first-half-hour->last-half-hour index momentum is real; 9:30-9:45 has the widest spreads and most false breaks; the Jul 27 $300k QQQ open-print sweep was this failure). On the exit side, the HL premium stop executed 14 seconds after the open at -67.6% vs its -50% width while the underlying was UP — the Jul 23 junk one-sided-quote mode on open-auction option marks, costing $3,650 (30% of Aug 20's loss). Shift _next_open_utc's armed cycle to open+30min so the first slate sees a formed opening range, and require the watchdog premium stop to see two consecutive 30s ticks breaching, never triggering on marks in the first 15 minutes.
changes.expected_effect: Eliminates open-print chases and quote-artifact option stops (~$3.7k saved on one incident alone); first-cycle entries get RVOL/range-confirmed prices per the ORB 'stocks in play' evidence (Sharpe 2.81 source effect).
changes.risk: Delays morning defense by up to 30 min on true gap-downs — mitigated by leaving sells, watchdog equity stops, and NAME FALLING exits fully live (only new entries and option premium-stop marks are deferred); a real -50% premium breach gets stopped ~1 minute later, not never.
changes.measurement: Next-run trades.jsonl entry timestamps: zero new-position fills 13:30-14:00 UTC; zero watchdog premium stops in the first 15 minutes; count of premium stops executing >5pp past OPTION_STOP_LOSS_PCT should go to zero.

changes.title: Close the options bypass of the anti-chase gate and bias convexity to single-leg calls (risk.evaluate_option, risk.py:903-1038)
changes.rationale: Options are the single largest leak: -$22,149 cycle (vs equity +$29,180), with bull_call_spreads 0-for-4 (-$33,794) and the only winner a single-leg MSFT long call (+$11,645). The HL trade documented its own gate bypass — equity blocked as overextended at RSI 70/4.2xATR, the identical thesis expressed via a $5,200 spread that lost -67.6% in 21 hours — and autotune is structurally blind here (no swept knob touches options). Fix: run the underlying through the same anti-chase check the equity path uses (RSI>=65 AND >=2.0 ATR haircut, >=3.0 ATR/gap hard block) inside evaluate_option, and add a decision-prompt line preferring long_call over bull_call_spread within the existing 1%-equity premium cap.
changes.expected_effect: Removes the overextension-bypass entry channel that produced HL (-$3,650) and rhymes with PLTR (-$9,940); shifts remaining option expressions toward the structure that actually won; options sleeve moves from -$22k drag toward breakeven-or-convex.
changes.risk: Fewer convexity trades overall and long calls consume more premium per unit of exposure than spreads (bounded by MAX_OPTION_PREMIUM_PCT=1); n=4 on the spread verdict is small, so this is a bias, not a spread ban.
changes.measurement: Next run: zero option entries on underlyings failing the anti-chase check (grep entry rationales vs gate logs); bull_call_spread count and P&L vs long_call count and P&L; options sleeve net P&L vs the -$18,606 away baseline.

changes.title: Pyramiding release: waive the +0.05 top-up conviction delta when the existing lot is in profit and passes anti-chase
changes.rationale: The one quantified 'block that COST' in the autopsy: Aug 18 'REJECT buy CDE: Top-up conviction 0.66 shows no new edge over prior entry 0.63 (needs +0.05)' — CDE rose +13.07% the next day and the foregone top-up was worth $7-12k. With a 31% win rate carried entirely by 2.4x payoff asymmetry (avg win $6,083 vs loss -$2,485), expectancy scales with winner size, and the top-up evidence gate as written can only add to names where conviction rose, which anti-selects against steadily-working winners. Release TOPUP_MIN_CONVICTION_DELTA (config default 0.05, add as explicit .env knob per the config digest's warning) when the lot's unrealized gain >= +5% AND the anti-chase gate passes, leaving the 4h MIN_ADD_INTERVAL, 8% daily symbol deploy, and 18% symbol caps fully binding.
changes.expected_effect: Converts the existing winner pipeline into larger winners: one CDE-class add per window at historical hit rates adds ~$3-8k; raises avg win above $6,083 without new-name risk.
changes.risk: n=1 supporting incident, and it feeds the concentration pattern the nightlies flagged 5 of 8 nights (CDE was already a $112k double lot driving 75% of Aug 19's bounce) — the anti-chase pass requirement and untouched 18%/8% caps are the containment; if next-run top-up P&L is negative, revert first.
changes.measurement: Count of gate-released top-ups next run and their standalone realized P&L (tag them in the ledger rationale); avg win vs $6,083; max single-name exposure stays <=18%.

do_not_do: Do not tighten MIN_CONVICTION or MIN_NEW_NAME_CONVICTION: autotune W33/W34 swept every candidate (0.35-0.6 new-name, 0.1-0.3 global) and found 0 trades affected — every loser cleared the floors comfortably (QNT/LFTO >0.6, HL 0.63), and cycle low-conviction (<0.62) actually beat high (+$830 vs -$283/trade). The problem is signal composition, which change #1 addresses.

Do not arm COMPOSITE_GATE_ENABLED / raise MIN_COMPOSITE_SCORE as a floor: the composite is inverted at the TOP (Q4 >=2.02 expectancy -$859 cycle, -$1,792 away; Q3 1.60-1.99 is the best bucket at +$2,728) — a floor gates the wrong tail and would remove profitable Q1/Q3 trades while keeping the losing Q4 names.

Do not touch equity stop geometry (DEFAULT_STOP_LOSS_PCT=8, VOL_STOP_MULT, clamps): curated lesson 14's 'tighten stops so lots can't lose 30-40%' inherits the AMZN/HL misattribution — both were watchdog OPTION premium stops ledgered under the underlying ticker, firing as configured. The Jul 25 sweep already validated equity geometry, and all Aug 18 cuts landed 0.7-4.2pp before hard stops.

Do not add standing/always-on index puts or force put volume as an alpha fix for down-capture: the evidence digest grades bought index puts as the single most evidence-against technique researched (PPUT 32-yr record = a 36.5/63.5 equity-cash mix, pure premium drag), and the Aug 19 MARA puts the funnel declined would have lost (MARA +7.7%/+15.5%). Down-capture belongs to the regime/de-gross lens, not this plan.

changes.title: Pre-register a frozen 2-week eval window with a mechanical GO/NO-GO contract (commit contract file before day 1)
changes.rationale: Expectancy swung +$1,455/trade (pre-eval, N=20) to +$189 (away, N=18) to +$167 (cycle, N=42) purely on sample noise: win-rate CI is +/-21.5pp at N=20 (research_evidence). The honest math: 21 trades (skew-adjusted MinTRL) to 24 trades for a 95% one-sided positive-expectancy verdict, 33 for two-sided, 46 for 99%; at the cycle's realized rate (~42 closes/19 sessions ~ 2.2/day) a 2-week window yields ~20-25 closes — barely enough for ONE 95% one-sided expectancy verdict and nothing else. Every mid-window PR resets the clock and adds a Deflated-Sharpe 'trial'. Capture ratio must also be pre-defined: it flipped from FAIL (aug3_21 down_capture 2.306, 8 down days) to pass (away up 2.025/down 1.706) on a 3-up/4-down-day sample — day-level capture on <6 days per side is noise.
changes.expected_effect: First statistically interpretable window since the project started. Pre-registered pass criteria: (a) N>=24 closed trades, (b) expectancy>0 at 95% one-sided (t=mean/(sd/sqrt(N))>1.645 on realized_pl), (c) combined up+down capture >1.0 computed only if >=6 up AND >=6 down SPY days, (d) max drawdown > -5%. GO-to-live ($100-1000) requires TWO consecutive passing frozen windows (>=46 cumulative trades, the 99% bar) — one window can never authorize live money.
changes.risk: Known bleeds (bullish-only funnel 0/83 conversions, aug3_21 down-capture 2.31) run unfixed for the window. Acceptable: paper money, and the halt stack (daily loss 3%, drawdown 15%, risk.py:94) caps tail damage; the expectancy gate already saved ~$17k on KALU alone on Aug 18.
changes.measurement: At window close, recompute the four contract stats from state/trades.jsonl + state/equity_history.jsonl with the same plain-python method the verify_recompute agent used; verdict is whatever the committed contract file says, no post-hoc metrics admitted. Git log proves zero .env/risk.py/prompt commits inside the window.

changes.title: Fix the MLEG exit-backfill ledger bug and ledger options under their own OCC symbols (ship BEFORE window starts)
changes.rationale: The two realized-P&L ledgers disagree materially, so per panel rules neither headline is currently trustworthy: trades.jsonl says +$7,030.97 cycle realized vs broker-implied +$5,965.92 (delta $1,065.05 = 18% of the broker figure), traced to recon_null_pl_sell_records=2 from the Aug 17 AMZN 5-leg unwind — one with literal symbol "None" and exit_price -1.19. Separately, equity_history day_pl rows fail to telescope with equity snapshots by $686.62. Because options are ledgered under the underlying ticker, autotune is structurally blind to the two largest losses of the window (AMZN -$14,956, HL -$3,650) and the nightly postmortem misdiagnosed both as equity stop-width failures.
changes.expected_effect: Ledger-vs-broker delta collapses to ~$0; every sell row has non-null realized_pl and a real symbol; options become a visible, separately attributable asset class in autotune sweeps and cited-signal attribution (currently options n=5 -$22,149 vs equity n=37 +$29,180 is only recoverable by manual forensics).
changes.risk: Backfill schema change could double-count or orphan the two existing bad rows; migrate them explicitly rather than reprocessing. This is a measurement PR, not strategy — it does not violate the freeze if merged before window day 1.
changes.measurement: Next window's reconciliation shows recon_null_pl_sell_records=0 and abs(ledger-broker delta) < $5; autotune 2026-W36+ report lists option trades in its own bucket; day_pl telescoping gap < $1.

changes.title: Harden watchdog option premium-stop marks against junk open-auction quotes (monitor/watchdog.py, ship BEFORE window)
changes.rationale: The HL premium stop executed at -67.6% vs its -50% OPTION_STOP_LOSS_PCT width 14 seconds after the open (hl_seconds_after_open=14, overshoot 17.6pp) while the underlying traded UP — the documented Jul 23 one-sided-quote failure mode; PR #40 hardened entry pricing only. This is an evaluation-validity problem, not just a loss: the entire options sample (cycle n=5, -$22,149; bull_call_spread 0-for-4 -$33,794) is contaminated by artifact executions, so NO verdict on the options sleeve is possible until exit marks are validated. Fix in the watchdog's premium stop check: require two consecutive 30s ticks beyond threshold AND a two-sided quote (bid>0, spread <= the existing 10% cap already used at entry), and suppress premium-stop fires in the first 5 minutes after open.
changes.expected_effect: Option stops fire on real marks; the next window's options P&L becomes attributable to strategy rather than quote plumbing. Removes an estimated $3,650 (30% of Aug 20's -$11,970) class of artifact loss.
changes.risk: A genuine fast gap could take 30-60s longer to stop out, costing a few hundred dollars per event — bounded because every option position is a defined-risk debit (max_option_premium_pct=1% of equity). Watchdog-callback deadlock is a known hazard from Jul 27; keep the change inside the existing tick loop.
changes.measurement: Next window logs show zero premium-stop executions more than ~5pp past the -50% threshold, and every option-stop log line includes the validating two-sided quote; grep the window's logs for the '-6x%' overshoot signature.

changes.title: Fix nightly postmortem attribution to close-to-close marks and prune the corrupted curated.md lines
changes.rationale: The self-evaluation stream — the input to every future strategy decision — is corrupted: the Aug 18 postmortem called IESC 'the winner +$1,194' when IESC was the day's single biggest hit (-$6,693 close-to-close), because it measures realized P&L from entry basis and is blind to give-back. curated.md line 8 contradicts line 9, line 14 ('tighten stop width so lots cannot lose >30-40%') inherits the AMZN/HL options misattribution and would fight the deliberately backtested DEFAULT_STOP_LOSS_PCT=8.0, and line 11's sole supporting example (CDE) became the window's best trade (+$15,860). Any planner or prompt consuming curated.md raw imports these errors.
changes.expected_effect: Lessons name the actual largest daily contributors; curated.md stops feeding contradictory/hindsight-wrong guidance into future decisions and into the human's judgment. Cross-referencing fixed lessons with autotune also recovers suppressed signal (the INTC re-entry finding appeared independently in both streams).
changes.risk: Over-pruning loses valid nuggets — annotate lines 8/11/14 as superseded with the reason rather than deleting; the postmortem change touches reporting only, zero trading-path risk.
changes.measurement: On the next red day, the lesson file's named worst contributor matches an independent close-to-close attribution recompute (the red_day_autopsy method); curated.md contains no internally contradictory pair and no stop-width claims sourced from option premium stops.

changes.title: Restore Robinhood screener auth and make feed-liveness a pre-registered validity condition of the window
changes.rationale: The away window was silently confounded: RH OAuth died 2026-08-19T13:31:28Z and 'robinhood screener disabled (no credentials); skipping' appears from Aug 20 — two of the five SCREENER_SOURCES (robinhood, robinhood_scans) vanished mid-sample, changing slate generation, while the Claude babysit was auth-dead from Aug 17 and absent after Aug 21, so nothing detected it. A controlled eval window requires constant inputs; a feed dying mid-window is a confound that must invalidate or flag the sample, not degrade it silently.
changes.expected_effect: The next window runs on the same discovery stack end-to-end, or is automatically declared confounded. User action: run the existing RH browser re-auth runbook (commit 0998aac) before day 1; add one status line/flag per decision cycle asserting all five SCREENER_SOURCES healthy, consumed by the eval contract.
changes.risk: Depends on a user action (browser re-auth); if skipped, the window must be pre-declared as 'RH-less configuration' up front — which is itself a valid frozen config, just a different one than the away window ran.
changes.measurement: grep of the window's logs shows zero 'robinhood screener disabled' lines (or, if RH-less was declared, 8/8 days consistent); robinhood_health.json shows auth alive on every market day.

changes.title: Hold cadence and cost constant; audit the impossible cache-ledger numbers
changes.rationale: Cost discipline is already won and must not become a variable: away window cost $12.51 total ($0.192/decision, cycle P&L-to-spend 209:1). The cadence-bump precondition (cache_read>0) has been met since Jul 23, but bumping DECISION_INTERVAL_SECONDS=3120 mid-evaluation resets the sample clock, changes decision frequency (a strategy variable), and multiplies cost ($22->$83/mo at 15-min). Meanwhile api_usage.jsonl shows cache_read=7,297 constant with cache_write=0 on calls 52-60 minutes apart — arithmetically impossible under the default 5-min TTL — so the cost ledger's own accounting may be wrong and must be verified before it gates any future cadence decision.
changes.expected_effect: One less confound in the window; a trustworthy per-call cost figure ($0.151-0.192 currently disagrees across digest sections) and a documented explanation of the TTL/cache accounting before the deferred cadence decision is ever re-opened.
changes.risk: None to trading — read-only audit of engine cache_control ttl and api_usage.jsonl writer; the only cost is foregoing the (unproven) benefit of faster cycles for two more weeks.
changes.measurement: A written reconciliation of observed cache_read/cache_write against the configured TTL, cross-checked against one day of Anthropic console usage; window cost lands at ~$0.19/decision x ~80 calls = ~$15 +/- 20%.

diagnosis: The headline numbers materially disagree and per panel rules none should be trusted yet: trades.jsonl says +$7,031 cycle realized vs broker-implied +$5,966 (delta $1,065, traced to two null-P&L MLEG backfill rows including a literal symbol="None"), and the away window shows +$3,403 realized while equity fell $10,689-$11,376 — the equity curve, not the trade ledger, is currently the only honest series. Expectancy "collapsed" from +$1,455 to +$189/trade between adjacent windows, but at N=18-20 the win-rate CI is +/-21.5pp, so both numbers are the same distribution sampled twice; the math says 24 closed trades for a 95% one-sided expectancy verdict, 33 two-sided, 46 at 99% — one frozen ~2.5-3.3-week window per verdict, and every mid-window PR resets the clock while adding a multiple-testing trial. Worse, the self-evaluation loop is corrupted: the postmortem labeled IESC "winner +$1,194" on the day it was the biggest hit (-$6,693 close-to-close), both mega-losses (AMZN -$14,956, HL -$3,650) were option premium stops misdiagnosed as equity stop-width failures, autotune's five swept knobs cannot see options at all, and the HL stop itself executed on a junk open-auction quote 17.6pp past its width — so the largest loss channel is part measurement artifact. Cost is a solved problem ($0.192/decision, 209:1 P&L-to-spend) and the deterministic risk layer demonstrably earns its keep (KALU/AEHR expectancy-gate rejects saved ~$17k+ on Aug 18); the binding constraints are ledger integrity and sample size, not ideas or spend.
do_not_do: Do not act on ANY subgroup finding below the 21-trade MinTRL: the composite-Q4 inversion (n~10, 8/10 losers), the conviction-band flip (sign reversed between windows on n=5 vs 13), the insider-cited kill (n=13, -$18,681), or killing bull call spreads outright (0-for-4 where 2 of 4 losses include quote-artifact executions) — instrument and track them in the fixed ledger instead; also respect autotune's own 5-trade bar and leave REENTRY_PRICE_OVERRIDE_COMPOSITE at 1.25 (the 1.5 finding is n=1).

Do not bump DECISION_INTERVAL_SECONDS (3120) or the decision model/effort during the window, even though the cache_read>0 precondition has been satisfied since Jul 23 — it resets the eval clock, multiplies cost 4x, and the only documented intraday edge (first-half-hour predicts last-half-hour, R2 1.6%) argues for close-management, not more entry cycles.

Do not feed curated.md to the prompt or to planners until lines 8/9 (contradiction), 11, and 14 (options misattribution, CDE counterexample) are pruned — consuming it raw imports the wrong lessons the postmortem bug generated.

Do not schedule any live-money deployment decision off the next window alone: a single 2-week window (~20-25 trades) can at best support one 95% one-sided expectancy claim with a +/-21.5pp win-rate CI; GO for $100-1000 live requires two consecutive passing frozen windows (>=46 cumulative trades) under the pre-registered contract, with a reconciled ledger, per the base-rate reality that 74-97% of comparable retail operations lose money.
lens: PROCESS-FIRST: evaluation rigor, sample-size honesty, measurement integrity, cost discipline, anti-overfitting
